service.label: Never miss a call
service.sell: making sure you never miss a call
service.verb: set up missed-call text back and online booking
service.why: A caller who reaches voicemail often calls the next business on the list. A text back keeps the conversation going.
service.offer: I'd like to send you a free one-page missed-call plan for {biz}: the text your business would send when you miss a call, an after-hours reply, a booking flow and answers to the questions callers ask, all written from your website.
service.ask: Want me to send it over?
service.walkin: Could I leave you a free one-page plan for the calls you miss? It's written from your own website and takes me a day.
service.follow1: Floating this back up. The free missed-call plan for {biz} is still yours if you want it: the text your number would send when you miss a call, written from your website.
service.subject: When {biz} misses a call

missed_call_facts.line: About 27% of calls to home services businesses go unanswered, and fewer than 3% of callers sent to voicemail leave a message.

missed_call_facts.line: Only 52% of callers to home services businesses reached a person.

missed_call_facts.line: In June 2025, 14.1% of calls to residential HVAC businesses came in after hours.

missed_call_facts.line: 65% of home service businesses don't show their hours online, 74% have no FAQ and 43% don't clearly list their service area.
missed_call_facts.label: Jobber survey of 1,050 owners, December 2025

missed_call_facts.line: On Google Local Services Ads, a call missed during business hours is a charged lead when the caller stays on the line over 20 seconds.
missed_call_facts.label: Google's Local Services Ads rule

texting_rules.rule: A text back answers a call the customer made, so keep it about that call: who it is, one question, the booking link, how to stop.
Every first text says how to stop. STOP, QUIT, END, CANCEL, UNSUBSCRIBE, REVOKE and OPT OUT all count; honor them right away (the rule allows 10 business days at most).
No promotions to people who only called. Promotional texts need written consent.
Register the business number for texting (A2P 10DLC) under the client's business before going live; approval usually takes under a week.
An AI voice never makes outbound calls without consent; it only answers.

recording.line: If calls are recorded, the greeting says so: "This call may be recorded." Some states need every party's consent, and callers can be anywhere.
recording.note: Digital Media Law Project list (page no longer updated). Federal law is one-party consent (18 U.S.C. 2511). Check your state.

job_checklist: Signed agreement, and the client's facts in writing: business name, hours, services, service area, emergency policy, booking link, prices they're happy to share, who gets alerts.
Every account in the client's name (texting or answering tool, booking page). You are added as a user. Nothing on your card.
Register texting (A2P 10DLC) under the client's business before going live.
Paste the missed-call text, the after-hours text and the FAQ answers. Read them out loud with the owner.
Set conditional forwarding so only missed calls go to the answering line. The client keeps their number.
If calls are recorded, add the recording notice to the greeting.
Test from two phones: a call during hours, a call after hours, a STOP reply, a test booking, and the alert reaching the owner.
Go live. Send the owner the setup sheet with every login, setting and monthly cost.
Every week: read the texts, fix wrong answers, check the booking link.
Every month: send the one-page report with the numbers from their tools.

objections.reply: You do, and that's why customers like you. This only kicks in on the calls you can't pick up: when you're on a roof, under a sink or asleep. You keep your number.
Agreed. It starts with a text from your business, signed with your name, asking what they need. Anyone who wants you still gets your call back.
Fair. Compare the monthly price with one job you'd lose to the next number on the list. Try the first month, and cancel any month.

objections.objection: We already use Jobber or Housecall Pro.
objections.reply: Even better. I'll set up the answering and texting features in the tool you already pay for and keep the answers up to date.
Replying to someone who just called you is a conversation they started. Your number gets registered for texting, every first text says how to stop, and STOP is honored right away.

objections.objection: I don't want to change my number.
objections.reply: You don't. Only the calls you miss get forwarded, and you can switch it off with one code.

first_clients.founding_terms: Setup free and the first 3 months of care at half price. The ask: honest feedback, a testimonial the member may quote (said plainly as a founding client when quoted) and permission to show before and after numbers (no names unless they say yes). Never a review: reviews are asked for separately, with nothing attached.
first_clients.step_up: After 3 founding clients, the setup fee starts. After 6, full price on everything.
first_clients.why: judgment call: the first 3 buy proof, not profit. A case study with real numbers sells the next 10.

promises: Live on your number within 7 days of getting access to your accounts, or your setup fee back.
If a test call or text ever fails, I fix it the same day.
No contract on the monthly care. Cancel any month.

where_buyers_look.channel: Contractor peer groups and online communities (for example EGIA's Contractor Connect)
Trade associations and their local chapters (ACCA for HVAC)
Free small business counseling: SBDC and SCORE
The field software they already use (Jobber, Housecall Pro) and its add-ons
Supply houses early in the morning

licenses.item: Business license or registration where you live
Texting registration (A2P 10DLC) for each client's number, on their account
Professional liability (E&O) insurance once you have paying clients: median about $110 a month for tech businesses (Insureon customers)
